attributes.source_locator: Abstract; section 2.3 'Length-invariant clock normalization'; section 4 'Sensitivity to the clock normalization hyperparameter'; Figure 2 and its caption; Table 5
attributes.value: The clock normalisation hyperparameter is omitted from the EvoFlows text and governs the realised edit budget. A sweep across both families and three seeds finds that a clock rate of approximately 95 replicates the published edit ratio of 0.43, while the reported evaluation uses 40 for a budget of about 5 edits, and a clock normalisation that optimises MMD sits around 80 or about 8.5 edits. Reconciling published and replicated edit distributions required reverse-engineering this parameter. The paper is not self-consistent about the replicating rate: the body gives approximately 95 while Figure 2's own annotation reads about 94, and neither value is reconciled with the other.

description: A descriptive statement the source makes, with the location it is printed at.
name: An undocumented clock normalisation sets the realised edit count

attributes.source_locator: Appendix C 'Interpolation Schedule Analysis'
attributes.value: The Edit Flows paper reports a cubic interpolation schedule in its narrative while its figure specifies a linear one with a code comment saying so. Both deposit identical total cross-entropy mass, but the linear schedule gives an expected kappa of 0.50 against 0.25 for the cubic, shifting supervision mass toward later times and raising the expected count of active edit targets per example from 32.7 to 50.1 across 400 homolog pairs. EditJumps adopts the linear schedule.

attributes.source_locator: Section 5, the paragraph beginning 'Furthermore, cross-study benchmarking frequently normalises scores'
attributes.value: Cross-study benchmarking frequently normalises scores. The paper reports that this holds for relative edit distance but fails for distributional estimators such as spectrum MMD: expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, 'a difference sufficiently large to invert method rankings'. Because both the numerator and the baseline floor contract with sample size, internal normalisation cannot replace standardised reference sets.

attributes.accelerator_details: A single NVIDIA L4 GPU for the primary training run
attributes.head: Three per-position operation rate heads for insertion, deletion and substitution and two token prediction heads, all conditioned by Feature-wise Linear Modulation on an MLP of a sinusoidal time embedding. Section 3 states linear rather than MLP rate heads for this arm.
attributes.hyperparameters: Fine-tuned for 20,000 steps, batch size 16, Adam, learning rate 1e-4; linear schedule kappa_t = t; frozen holding-interval rates; clock normalisation 40, chosen for a budget of about 5 edits; Euler tau-leaping with 50 steps.
limitations: The scored editor was trained for 20,000 steps of batch size 16, which the sources state saw about 19% of one epoch of the training corpus, and the paper states the model remained non-converged at that budget.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

The edit budget is calibrated in expectation, not guaranteed per sequence: the paper states that clock normalisation has no closed-form mapping to realised edits, so a specific budget requires empirical calibration rather than deterministic control.

Section 3 states this arm uses linear rate heads, while the released checkpoint's model card ships MLP rate heads and the ESM-2 masked language modelling head as the token head, so the scored arm and the downloadable weights are not stated to be the same configuration.

checkpoint_sha256.note: The paper names no checkpoint file for the scored arm, and the released weights are described with a different head parameterisation.

code_commit.note: The paper does not state the commit the reported runs were produced at.

comparison.adaptation: Zero-shot, one generalist editor
comparison.aggregation: Normalised against the natural homolog ceiling
comparison.budget: About 4 to 5 edits per sequence
comparison.dataset_version: Ty1 and HER2-VH, 200 references each
comparison.inputs: One seed amino-acid sequence per template and an approximate edit budget
comparison.metric_implementation: percent of the natural homolog ceiling
comparison.split: Two antibody families, 200 references each

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.

The scored editor is not a converged model. It was fine-tuned for 20,000 steps at batch size 16, which the model card gives as about 19% of one epoch, and Appendix D states the model remained non-converged at that budget, with validation loss still falling, 149.6 at step 8,500, 138.7 at step 16,000 and 135.2 at step 19,999.
attributes.protocol: Metrics normalised against the attainable ceiling computed on held-out natural homologs.

comparison.adaptation: Zero-shot: one generalist editor applied to a held-out target without per-family retraining
comparison.aggregation: Pooled over the 400 generated sequences of the family
comparison.budget: Clock normalisation 40, set for a budget of about 5 edits per sequence; Euler tau-leaping over 50 steps
comparison.dataset_version: HER2-VH homolog family mined from the paired Observed Antibody Space corpus at repository commit d827d47c3bcd29e0f4c15a15f9ac92a6cd859e99
comparison.inputs: One seed amino-acid sequence per template and an approximate edit budget
comparison.metric_implementation: residue covariance agreement against a 300-sequence natural homolog ceiling
comparison.split: 20 templates and 20 variants per template, 400 generated sequences, scored against 200 held-out HER2-VH homologs; agreement ceiling 300 real HER2-VH homologs

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
The EvoFlows paper specifies the covariance matrix but omits the scalar reduction, so the reduction scored here is the EditJumps authors' own choice.
The paper reports that this score moves with the reference partition alone, from 83.6% to 85.1%, and with the reference set size, from 0.790 at 20 references to 0.985 at 800.

The scored editor is not a converged model. It was fine-tuned for 20,000 steps at batch size 16, which the model card gives as about 19% of one epoch, and Appendix D states the model remained non-converged at that budget, with validation loss still falling, 149.6 at step 8,500, 138.7 at step 16,000 and 135.2 at step 19,999.
attributes.protocol: One frame for every arm and both families: 20 templates per family and 20 variants per template, so 400 generated sequences, scored against a 200-sequence held-out natural homolog set, with the agreement ceiling computed on 300 real homologs. Sampling runs Euler tau-leaping over 50 steps. Every arm is held to a matched realised edit budget of about 4 to 5 edits per sequence.

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
The EvoFlows paper specifies the covariance matrix but omits the scalar reduction, so the reduction scored here is the EditJumps authors' own choice.
The paper reports that this score moves with the reference partition alone, from 83.6% to 85.1%, and with the reference set size, from 0.790 at 20 references to 0.985 at 800.

Sampling runs Euler tau-leaping over 50 steps. Every arm is held to a matched realised edit budget of about 4 to 5 edits per sequence.

comparison.adaptation: Per-family retraining of a 650M trunk for 2,000 steps, then forced infilling
comparison.aggregation: Pooled over the 400 generated sequences of the family
comparison.budget: b = 5 on Ty1 and b = 4 on HER2-VH, guaranteed in a single pass
comparison.dataset_version: HER2-VH homolog family mined from the paired Observed Antibody Space corpus at repository commit d827d47c3bcd29e0f4c15a15f9ac92a6cd859e99
comparison.inputs: One template sequence, a per-column entropy profile from the family alignment and an edit budget
comparison.metric_implementation: positional entropy difference from the natural holdout; the target value is zero
comparison.split: 20 templates and 20 variants per template, 400 generated sequences, scored against 200 held-out HER2-VH homologs; agreement ceiling 300 real HER2-VH homologs

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
The EvoFlows paper names this metric without giving a definition or a scalar reduction, so the formulation scored here is the EditJumps authors' own choice.
attributes.protocol: One frame for every arm and both families: 20 templates per family and 20 variants per template, so 400 generated sequences, scored against a 200-sequence held-out natural homolog set, with the agreement ceiling computed on 300 real homologs. Sampling runs Euler tau-leaping over 50 steps. Every arm is held to a matched realised edit budget of about 4 to 5 edits per sequence.

comparison.aggregation: Pooled over the 400 generated sequences of the family
comparison.budget: Not budgeted: the distances are those between natural sequences, about 23 edits per pair
comparison.dataset_version: Ty1 homolog family mined from the paired Observed Antibody Space corpus at repository commit d827d47c3bcd29e0f4c15a15f9ac92a6cd859e99
comparison.inputs: Pairs of real family homologs
comparison.metric_implementation: per-position formulation chosen by the EditJumps authors, against a 200-sequence natural holdout
comparison.split: 20 templates and 20 variants per template, 400 generated sequences, scored against 200 held-out Ty1 homologs; agreement ceiling 300 real Ty1 homologs

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
The EvoFlows paper names this metric without giving a definition or a scalar reduction, so the formulation scored here is the EditJumps authors' own choice.
attributes.protocol: One frame for every arm and both families: 20 templates per family and 20 variants per template, so 400 generated sequences, scored against a 200-sequence held-out natural homolog set, with the agreement ceiling computed on 300 real homologs. Sampling runs Euler tau-leaping over 50 steps. Every arm is held to a matched realised edit budget of about 4 to 5 edits per sequence.

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
The EvoFlows paper specifies the matrix but omits the scalar reduction, so the reduction scored here is the EditJumps authors' own choice.
The paper reports that computing the ceiling in an unaligned or mismatched frame shifts this score by 2.3 percentage points.

The scored editor is not a converged model. It was fine-tuned for 20,000 steps at batch size 16, which the model card gives as about 19% of one epoch, and Appendix D states the model remained non-converged at that budget, with validation loss still falling, 149.6 at step 8,500, 138.7 at step 16,000 and 135.2 at step 19,999.
attributes.protocol: One frame for every arm and both families: 20 templates per family and 20 variants per template, so 400 generated sequences, scored against a 200-sequence held-out natural homolog set, with the agreement ceiling computed on 300 real homologs. Sampling runs Euler tau-leaping over 50 steps. Every arm is held to a matched realised edit budget of about 4 to 5 edits per sequence.

comparison.adaptation: Per-family retraining, which the original approach requires

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
Reference set size, split, templates, seeds and metric implementation behind these published values could not be recovered from the EvoFlows paper, so the comparison fields are unknown.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. Every pinned artifact was re-downloaded from the URL in its source record and its SHA-256 recomputed: all nine match. The arXiv PDF's text layer was regenerated with pdftotext -layout from poppler 26.08.0 and matches the hash notes.md records. npm run batch -- check-values over the whole batch reproduced the extractor's figures exactly (8 in_cell, 164 in_row, 3 locator_not_parsed, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row). Because 164 results sit at in_row only, column assignment was then checked separately by review/column_check.py, written for this pass and using neither extract/tables.py nor extract/check_tables.py. It builds two independent column models: the PDF text layer, where Tables 2 and 4 are assigned by clustering printed field right edges and Table 1 by ordinal position within the row, and the arXiv HTML rendering parsed as a cell grid from the table markup. The two models agree on every cell, and all 172 table-located results match their locator's column and block in both. Four negative controls, two columns exchanged within a row, a row shifted one column left, a Ty1 and HER2 sub-column exchanged, and the Table 1 upper and lower blocks exchanged for one row label, are rejected by both models.

entity_classification.rationale: The two columns of Table 4 are normalised against different ceilings, on different numbers of families and different reference sets, so each is its own protocol and the two must not be pooled.

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.

The paper states that ceilings are highly sensitive to the multiple sequence alignment projection: computing them in an unaligned or mismatched frame shifts mutual information product agreement by 2.3 percentage points, so ceilings only compare within one coordinate frame.
The two columns of Table 4 rest on different numbers of families and different reference sets, so they are not a like-for-like comparison.

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.

description: Maximum mean discrepancy between the k-mer spectra of the generated set and a natural reference set. Printed by the EvoFlows paper under conditions the replication states it could not recover, so none of this protocol's comparison fields is known.
name: EvoFlows published values, two families: MMD

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.

The scored editor is not a converged model. It was fine-tuned for 20,000 steps at batch size 16, which the model card gives as about 19% of one epoch, and Appendix D states the model remained non-converged at that budget, with validation loss still falling, 149.6 at step 8,500, 138.7 at step 16,000 and 135.2 at step 19,999.

attributes.source_locator: Appendix E 'Sample-Size Dependency and Grounded Baseline Controls', the sentence beginning 'Scoring real homologs against real homologs'

description: One value printed in the body text of Appendix E, where the covariance agreement between two sets of natural homologs is reported at three reference-set sizes.
name: Natural homologs against natural homologs, covariance agreement, 800 references

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
The EvoFlows paper specifies the covariance matrix but omits the scalar reduction, so the reduction scored here is the EditJumps authors' own choice.
The paper reports that this score moves with the reference partition alone, from 83.6% to 85.1%, and with the reference set size, from 0.790 at 20 references to 0.985 at 800.

The scored editor is not a converged model. It was fine-tuned for 20,000 steps at batch size 16, which the model card gives as about 19% of one epoch, and Appendix D states the model remained non-converged at that budget, with validation loss still falling, 149.6 at step 8,500, 138.7 at step 16,000 and 135.2 at step 19,999.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.

attributes.source_locator: Table 2, family block "her2vh", row "EditJumps", column "ΔH"

description: One printed cell of Table 2, the reimplemented block scored against a 200-sequence natural holdout.
name: EditJumps on HER2-VH, ΔH, 200 references

limitations: Computational distribution comparison only. The value measures how similar generated sequences are to a reference set of natural sequences; it is not a measured binding affinity, specificity, stability or retained function.

Scores depend on the size of the reference set. Expanding the reference alignment from 200 to 800 homologs alters the normalised spectrum MMD ratio by 50% on Ty1 and 26% on HER2-VH, which the paper states is large enough to invert method rankings, so the ordering of methods is not stable across reference-set sizes.

113 of Ty1's and 103 of HER2-VH's 200 reference sequences were present in the training set. Re-evaluating with strictly disjoint reference sets shifted spectrum MMD by -36.7% on Ty1 and -12.6% on HER2-VH and increased covariance agreement by 12 to 17 points.

The two held-out targets are single-chain constructs, the camelid VHH Ty1 and the isolated heavy chain HER2-VH, while the training pairs are concatenated two-chain VH.VL sequences. The paper names this as a domain shift.

Aggregate similarity is substantially driven by conserved framework scaffolds. 76% of residues are framework and 24% are complementarity-determining regions, and within those regions the model closes under 25% of the gap between random mutation and natural homologs, so a high aggregate score is not evidence of a better antigen-binding loop.
Seed values are not printed. Table 1's caption says it reports individual runs and intervals across three seeds; Table 2 prints one value per cell with no interval.

The paper states that its computed values and the published EvoFlows values are not comparable and that it could not recover the original experimental conditions from the EvoFlows paper. Table 1's caption adds that the two blocks are not comparable and that each row compares only against its own block's floor and ceiling.
The EvoFlows paper names this metric without giving a definition or a scalar reduction, so the formulation scored here is the EditJumps authors' own choice.

The scored editor is not a converged model. It was fine-tuned for 20,000 steps at batch size 16, which the model card gives as about 19% of one epoch, and Appendix D states the model remained non-converged at that budget, with validation loss still falling, 149.6 at step 8,500, 138.7 at step 16,000 and 135.2 at step 19,999.
